headline: Steady enrollment growth offset by seasonal summer softness
summary_short: Grand Canyon Education's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 6.7% y/y to $264.0M and net income grew 10.4% y/y to $45.9M ($1.75 diluted EPS), but both fell sharply sequentially (-14.5% revenue, -39.1% net income) on the normal summer enrollment dip.
summary_long: Revenue grew 6.7% y/y to $264.0M as university-partner enrollments rose 7.6% to 126,231, partly offset by a slight decline in revenue per student from a partner contract change and mix shift. Technology/academic and counseling costs rose on higher headcount and compensation; marketing spend rose on new-site advertising; G&A fell 11.4% on lower legal fees. Net income rose 10.4% y/y to $45.9M ($1.75 diluted EPS, +18.2% y/y, aided by a smaller share count from buybacks). Sequentially, revenue and profit fell sharply — the company attributes this to normal summer seasonality, when fewer GCU ground students take courses against largely fixed costs. Cash was $171.1M; GCE repurchased $76.0M of stock in the quarter and continues to plan $30-35M of annual capex.
